source.title: A Cross-Architecture Audit of Direction-Based Inference-Time Defences in Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Xiang-Yu Yin; Tora Bodin; Rohan Menon; Chih-Hong Cheng

page_placements.theme: Cross-modality: text-derived refusal direction applied to image, video, audio and VLA inputs

record.tranche_reason: The study applies one-layer, norm-controlled direction subtractions and measures refusal, including a text-only refused-versus-complied direction. This tests related causal-direction claims using a different intervention and in vision-language models, rather than reproducing the original all-layer, all-position ablation and addition.
record.gate_note: The paper tests text-only CMRM-like refusal-direction subtraction, image-conditioning-direction subtraction, and cross-model transfer. Rows for image-conditioning subtraction and its random control are recorded under fits_no_version because that direction is an image-versus-text conditioning shift, not the harmful-versus-harmless or refused-versus-complied refusal direction named in the versions. The cross-paradigm cosine alignment is reported in the text and figure, but does not test whether the direction mediates refusal.
record.test_reason: In five VLMs, the study steers activations with a text-only refused-vs-complied (CMRM-like) direction at one layer and reports refusal rates against a matched-norm random control. That bears on V1's claim that the direction causally controls refusal, in a new multimodal setting. It is not a T1/T2 replication. The direction is refused-vs-complied rather than harmful-vs-harmless, it is applied at one layer with ABL_POS-matched magnitude, and it is used to raise refusal on jailbreak-image prompts, not to ablate refusal. The cross-model transfer test uses the image-conditioning direction, not a refusal direction, so it does not test V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Precisely: no single direction-based defence Pareto-dominates; selection and calibration should be per language-decoder family. The text-only CMRM refusal direction partially aligns with the image-conditioning shift on all 15 cells. The image-conditioning direction, not the refusal direction, fails to transfer across LLaVA-1.5-13B/Pixtral-12B.
record.recipe_differences: Uses one-layer, magnitude-controlled subtraction rather than projection at every layer and position; studies VLM image-conditioning shifts and a CMRM-like refused-versus-complied direction; does not test direction addition. The direction transfer test is between two VLM architectures.
record.method_sensitivity: Refusal recovery from ABL_POS rises monotonically across the three probed layer depths in all five model families; the direction-transfer test fails across the tested LLaVA-1.5-13B/Pixtral-12B pair. The paper also reports that a different refusal judge changes absolute rates but preserves the direction-specificity pattern.

fits_no_version.finding: The ABL_POS image-conditioning direction does not transfer between LLaVA-1.5-13B and Pixtral-12B. The two directions are nearly orthogonal (cos ≤0.04), and transferred refusal stays at or below WITH_IMAGE (n=20).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image-conditioning shift directions in VLMs are architecture-specific and do not transfer between dimension-compatible models.

fits_no_version.finding: Subtracting the image-conditioning shift recovers refusal, direction-specifically on 13/15 cells against matched-norm random control, with little MMBench utility loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing the image-conditioning shift at one layer recovers refusal to image jailbreaks in VLMs, depending on model and layer.

fits_no_version.finding: The text-only refusal direction has positive cosine with the multimodal image-conditioning shift on all 15 cells (mean 0.35, range 0.17–0.65; sign test p≈3e-5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The text-only refusal direction partially overlaps the image-induced compliance shift in VLMs.

record.problems: The paper tests five open-weight VLMs and one dimension-compatible model pair for transfer; closed-source models are not covered. Refusal uses a first-step substring lexicon that can miss paraphrased refusals, and MMBench MCQ is a coarse capability proxy. Transfer is based on n = 20 prompts per pair, with Wilson half-width ∼ 0.22. Two cells do not pass the uncorrected direction-specificity criterion, and utility gaps near the measurement noise floor warrant caution.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the tested V1 and V6 results. For the image-conditioning intervention, the separate MMBench utility values per model and layer in Tables 14 and 15 are not extracted individually; the aggregate reported in Table 5 and summarized in the text is recorded instead. Other defence candidates (IGNORE_INSTR and ShiftDC-like) were not catalogued because they do not test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Harmful-minus-harmless direction; ablation at all layers/positions removing refusal; adding the direction to harmless prompts; capability under the refusal-direction intervention (not extracted as rows). The sign convention of the CMRM-like direction is not stated explicitly.
No test of whether the attacks suppress the text refusal direction. The cosine alignment hints at overlap but is not a causal test. No adversarial training.
Harm judgment is not separated from the refusal decision.
Transfer of the refusal direction across languages, models or base/instruct is not tested. Only the image-conditioning direction is transferred.

missing.what: CMRM-like MMBench utility per cell (CN n=98 and EN n=190). Mean loss +0.001±0.026; the columns are identical to ABL_POS in both tables, which may be a reporting error. Bears on V1's 'other abilities kept'.
CMRM-like refusal by attack benchmark (FigStep 0.561, HADES 0.495, JailBreakV 0.618, MM-SB 0.185 vs WITH_IMAGE 0.409/0.313/0.440/0.046)
Cosine of the CMRM refusal direction with the image shift per cell (mean 0.35)

record.verdict_notes: The record marked CMRM rows 'reversed' because refusal rose under 'subtraction'. In this paper the subtraction is a defence intended to recover refusal, and rdir aligns positively with the compliance-ward image shift. Its effective action is therefore refusal-ward, analogous to V1's addition. The sign is inferred, not stated, so the verdicts carry that caveat. Table 11/13 rates mix calibration and held-out prompts. The V6 'challenges' label is removed because the transferred vector is the image-conditioning shift.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original harmful-minus-harmless direction exactly; does not project the direction out of every layer and position, add it to induce refusals to harmless requests, or test general capability under subtraction of the CMRM-like direction.
No conversion of the ablation into a weight edit or test of released-model abliteration.
Does not test whether jailbreak attacks suppress the direction or whether training against ablation improves robustness.
Partial cosine alignment between two directions is reported, but the study does not test affine refusal geometry, cones, or a dominant direction plus additional refusal directions.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Tests transfer only between LLaVA-1.5-13B and Pixtral-12B at matched layers; does not test transfer across languages, base-to-instruct models, or other model pairs.
Does not vary refusal training data, method, or timing.

relation.reason: Its own Table 13 refusal rates for the CMRM-like refusal direction, set against Table 11's random control, bear on whether the direction causally moves refusal.

tranche.reason: New setting: five VLMs, jailbreak-image prompts, one-layer subtraction of a text-only refused-vs-complied direction. It reports refusal rates against a matched-norm random control. The study is a defence audit, not a different method aimed at V1's question, so T3 fits better than the reader's T2.

source_check.notes: The CMRM-like refusal rates (Tables 11/13) come from a run mixing calibration and held-out prompts, with no per-cell CI. The paper does say refusal recovery uses n = 47–65 per cell. The direction's sign is not stated: Fig. 1(a) plots |cos| and the text says refused-vs-complied, so the refusal-ward reading rests on the defence framing and the §5.3 refusal-to-compliance explanation. The CMRM-like utility columns in Table 14 and the English MMBench table are identical to ABL_POS cell by cell (likely a copy error), so the capability-cost evidence for the refusal direction is unreliable.

statements.problem: none; 13/15 uses uncorrected per-cell 95% CIs (11/15 under Bonferroni)
